blocks.html:
Build reports, notices, and guides from semantic HTML and CSS. Fullbleed renders tagged PDF output with embedded fonts, document metadata, and page previews you can inspect.

Read the accessibility workflow Get the C# starter

Start with a checked example

Riverton Library · C# and HTML/CSS

A fictional workshop notice with scoped table headers, an illustration and its description, and an editable HTML/CSS template. The stable C# starter includes source and retained validator reports for its PDF/UA-1 and PDF/UA-2 specimens.

Open the PDF/UA-1 notice · Open the PDF/UA-2 notice · C# source and checks

Common Ground · Python components

A fictional community-program guide with an illustrated cover, reusable program cards, and a captioned schedule. Its source and saved PDF come with structure checks and independent validator reports.

Open the Common Ground PDF · Python source and checks · View the HTML export

This retained source kit pins experimental Python 2.6.0a7. See the current component guide for the latest API and installation steps.

Build meaning into the source

  • Use real headings, lists, captions, and table headers with explicit relationships.

  • Write useful image descriptions and keep the source in a logical reading order.

  • Set the document title and language, and register embeddable fonts covering your text.

Verify the document you ship

  1. Render with the intended tagged-PDF profile and inspect every final page.

  2. Check the PDF structure and diagnostics, then run an independent validator such as veraPDF for the selected profile.

  3. Review reading order, alternative text, contrast, and usefulness with intended readers and assistive technology.

  4. Retain the exact PDF, source, assets, package versions, and validation reports together.

Repeat these checks after changing the content or design. A profile setting or passing machine check alone does not establish full PDF/UA or WCAG acceptance.

Working from scans?

First obtain reviewed text with a separate transcription or OCR workflow. Use that text to author a tagged alternative, and preserve the original record alongside it.
